title: Motherhood Isn’t Sacrifice; It’s Selfishness
titleZh: 母职不是牺牲，而是“自私”

paragraphs.A: I was taking a few weeks’ break from work over the summer. My family and I—my husband and my sons, then 9 and 7—planned to spend the time at our house on the New Jersey shore. When my mother asked what we would be doing on our vacation, I told her we would be together—going to the beach and the nearby amusement park, cooking, playing in the yard. In response, my mother said: “Oh, that’s not much of a vacation for you. I’ll bet you can’t wait to get back to work. Motherhood, it’s the hardest job in the world. All sacrifice!” “Really?” was all I could say in response.
paragraphs.B: I was looking forward to uninterrupted time with my boys. We would spend days by the ocean and take trips to the boardwalk, where they would scream with delight while riding the roller coaster—the same one I’d ridden when I was their age, then ridden alongside them until Hurricane Sandy deposited it into the Atlantic. We’d ram one another with bumper cars; we’d ride the old-fashioned merry-go-round, waiting until my youngest son’s favorite horse, bright-blue Freddy, became available. Some days were sure to end in tears of exhaustion, but the tears didn’t outweigh the joy. Even on the bad days.
paragraphs.C: My mother was only trying to be sympathetic to my life as a working mother, but the self-satisfied way she proclaimed the sacrificial nature of motherhood grated. I don’t believe for one second that motherhood is the hardest job in the world nor that it is all sacrifice. Still, it wasn’t fair to blame her; she was merely parroting a common refrain. Once my annoyance lifted, in its place spread a kind of clarity that helped me to understand how these linguistic tropes reinforce the disempowerment of mothers and women.
paragraphs.D: The assertion of motherhood as sacrifice comes with a perceived glorification. A woman is expected to sacrifice her time, ambition and sense of self to a higher purpose, one more worthy than her own individual identity. This leaves a vacuum in the place of her value, one that others rush to fill.
paragraphs.E: When a woman becomes pregnant, she seems to become public property. Perhaps because bearing children ensures the continuation of the species, it is often prioritized as part of a larger social contract. Not only does this logic lead to an attempt to legislate women’s bodies, but also in smaller, everyday gestures, boundaries get crossed. Many friends tell stories about being touched by strangers during pregnancy, as if a woman’s maternal status turns her into a vessel to handle.
paragraphs.F: Written more than 30 years ago, Margaret Atwood’s The Handmaid’s Tale offers a cautionary tale of womanhood as sacrifice. In this dystopic novel, women are grouped according to the uses men determine for them: namely, sterile wives married for appearance or fertile “handmaids,” who are raped routinely for procreation. One male character declares that the woman must “learn in silence with all subjection” and that “she shall be saved by childbearing.” In this scenario, the act of the concept of motherhood as sacrifice.
paragraphs.G: When we cling to the idea of motherhood as sacrifice, what we really sacrifice is our sense of self, as if it is the price we pay for having children.
paragraphs.H: Motherhood is not a sacrifice, but a privilege—one that many of us choose selfishly. At its most atavistic, procreating ensures that our genes survive into the next generation. You could call this selfishness a biological imperative. On a personal level, when we bring into the world a being that is of us, someone we will protect and love and for whom we will do everything we can to help thrive and flourish, it begets the question, How is this selfless? Selflessness implies that we have no skin in the game. In motherhood, we’re all in.
paragraphs.I: By reframing motherhood as a privilege, we redirect agency back to the mother, empowering her, celebrating her autonomy instead of her sacrifice. Granted, some of us have more autonomy than others. There are many mothers who would not have chosen motherhood, for financial or personal reasons. Still, by owning our roles as mothers and refusing the false accolades of martyrdom, we do more to empower all women.
paragraphs.J: In my experience, when women talk among women, our ambivalence or frustration is rarely about our roles as mothers. (That doesn’t mean our kids don’t drive us crazy sometimes.) Rather, conversations turn to questions of how to manage the best part of our lives (those very kids who are driving us crazy) with our partners, careers and other responsibilities. And while many women derive their deepest fulfillment as mothers, it doesn’t preclude their ambition or fly in the face of leaning in or out or sideways.
paragraphs.K: Calling motherhood “the hardest job in the world” misses the point completely because having and raising children is not a “job.” No one will deny that there is exhaustion, fear and tedium. Raising a family is hard work, but so is every other meaningful aspect of our lives.
paragraphs.L: The language surrounding child rearing as a job surely derived from caregivers’ and homemakers’ efforts to be acknowledged as fulfilling an important role. And clearly raising children is one of the most important things we do—for both women and men—but that does not make it a job. In a job, an employer pays for services an employee agrees to perform. And there is a boss to whom the employee reports. In the case of parenting, who would that be?
paragraphs.M: That doesn’t mean we don’t want support—paid parental leave, more flexible working hours, publicly funded day care. But the cultural shift has to happen for the policies to follow. Martyrs, after all, don’t need or expect public services.
paragraphs.N: Fathers are rarely, if ever, spoken about in the same way that mothers are. It’s culturally acceptable for men to have children and professional identities without having to choose between the two. These unspoken biases run deep. It reminds me of a friend whose husband complained about having to “babysit” the children while she went to dinner with friends. Has a woman ever “babysat” her own children? Things are changing, but the insidious inferences persist.
paragraphs.O: Further, with “women” and “family” as go-to cultural corollaries, studies show, terrifyingly, that these biases are being adopted by artificial intelligence, too. Calling motherhood a woman’s “job” only serves to keep a woman in her place. The priorities of mothers who work outside the home are often questioned. It’s as if women are forced to choose between ambition (or simply earning a living wage) and family.
paragraphs.P: If we start referring to motherhood as the beautiful, messy privilege that it is, and to tending to our children as the most loving yet selfish thing we do, perhaps we can change the biased language my mother used. Only when we stop talking about motherhood as sacrifice can we start talking about mothers the way that we deserve.

translationZh.A: 夏天，我休了几周假，打算和丈夫以及当时九岁、七岁的两个儿子一起，在新泽西海岸的家中度过。母亲问我们假期准备做什么，我说我们会一起去海滩和附近的游乐园、做饭、在院子里玩。母亲却说：“这对你可算不上什么假期。我猜你一定迫不及待地想回去工作。当母亲是世界上最辛苦的工作，全是牺牲！”我只能回答：“真的吗？”
translationZh.B: 我盼望着和孩子们不受打扰地相处。我们会在海边玩上好几天，去海滨木板路，在过山车上兴奋尖叫。那也是我小时候坐过、后来陪他们一起坐过的过山车，直到桑迪飓风把它卷入大西洋。我们会开碰碰车互相碰撞，坐老式旋转木马，等着小儿子最喜欢的亮蓝色小马弗雷迪空出来。有些日子难免因疲倦而以眼泪结束，但眼泪抵不过快乐，即便不顺心的日子也是如此。
translationZh.C: 母亲只是想体谅我作为职场母亲的生活，但她以一种自以为是的口气宣扬母职的牺牲性，令我不快。我丝毫不相信当母亲是世界上最辛苦的工作，也不相信它全是牺牲。不过，责怪她并不公平，她只是在重复一种常见论调。怒气消散后，我逐渐明白，这些语言比喻如何强化了母亲和女性缺乏自主权的处境。
translationZh.D: 把母职说成牺牲，似乎也是一种赞美。人们期望女性为一个比自身身份更崇高、更值得追求的目标，牺牲时间、抱负和自我意识。这使她自身价值的位置留下空白，而其他人争相填补。
translationZh.E: 女性一旦怀孕，仿佛就成了公共财产。也许因为生育能延续人类，它常被作为更广泛社会契约的一部分而优先考虑。这种逻辑不仅导致试图通过立法控制女性身体，也使日常生活中的细小举动越过边界。许多朋友说，怀孕时曾被陌生人触摸，仿佛母亲身份把女性变成了任人摆弄的容器。
translationZh.F: 玛格丽特·阿特伍德三十多年前写的《使女的故事》，警示了将女性身份视为牺牲的后果。在这部反乌托邦小说中，女性按男性决定的用途分类：一种是不育、为体面而迎娶的妻子，另一种是有生育能力、为繁殖而经常遭受强奸的“使女”。一名男性角色宣称，女性必须“安静地学习，一味顺服”，并称“她必因生育而得救”。本段最后一句在所提供的纸面原文中语句残缺，无法准确译出。
translationZh.G: 当我们执着于母职就是牺牲的观念时，真正牺牲的是自我意识，仿佛这是生育必须支付的代价。
translationZh.H: 母职不是牺牲，而是一种可贵的机会，许多人出于自身意愿选择它。从最原始的生物本能看，繁衍让我们的基因延续到下一代，可以说这种自利是生物本能。在个人层面，我们将一个源自自身的生命带到世上，保护和爱护他，尽一切努力帮助他茁壮成长。这引出一个问题：这怎么能算是无私呢？无私意味着自己并无切身利益，而在母职中，我们全身心投入。
translationZh.I: 将母职重新理解为一种可贵的机会，就能把自主权交还母亲，赋予她力量，赞赏她的自主选择而非牺牲。诚然，有些人的自主权更多。许多母亲出于经济或个人原因，本不会选择成为母亲。即便如此，通过掌握自己的母亲角色，拒绝殉道式牺牲的虚假赞誉，我们能更好地赋予所有女性力量。
translationZh.J: 依我的经验，女性之间谈话时，矛盾或挫败很少针对母亲角色本身。当然，孩子有时也会让我们抓狂。谈话更多围绕如何协调生活中最美好的部分——那些让我们抓狂的孩子——与伴侣、事业和其他责任。许多女性从母亲身份中获得最深的满足，但这并不排斥她们的抱负，也不与她们选择积极进取、暂时退出或转变方向相冲突。
translationZh.K: 称母职为“世界上最辛苦的工作”完全偏离了重点，因为生育和养育孩子并不是一份雇佣工作。没有人否认其中的疲惫、恐惧和乏味。养家确实辛苦，但生活中其他有意义的事情同样如此。
translationZh.L: 把育儿称作工作，想必源于照护者和家庭主妇希望其重要作用得到承认。显然，养育孩子是女性和男性所做的最重要的事情之一，但这并不会使它成为一份雇佣工作。在工作中，雇主付钱购买雇员同意提供的服务，雇员还要向上司汇报。那么在育儿中，这个上司是谁呢？
translationZh.M: 这并不意味着我们不需要支持，例如带薪育儿假、更灵活的工时和公共资金支持的托育。但文化观念必须先转变，政策才能跟进。毕竟，被塑造成一味牺牲的“殉道者”，既不需要也不期待公共服务。
translationZh.N: 父亲极少被用谈论母亲的方式谈论。文化上，男性可以同时拥有孩子和职业身份，无须二选一。这些未明说的偏见根深蒂固。我想起一位朋友，她和朋友外出吃饭时，丈夫抱怨自己不得不“替人看孩子”。女性照顾自己的孩子，曾被这样称呼过吗？事情正在改变，但隐蔽有害的暗示依然存在。
translationZh.O: 更令人担忧的是，研究表明，文化中将“女性”和“家庭”习惯性关联的偏见，也正在被人工智能吸收。把母职称为女性的“工作”，只会让女性被固定在传统位置上。外出工作的母亲，其生活重心经常遭到质疑，仿佛女性必须在抱负——甚至仅仅是挣到维持生活的工资——与家庭之间作出选择。
translationZh.P: 如果我们开始将母职称为它本来的样子——一种美好而又混乱的可贵体验，将照顾孩子称为我们所做的最有爱、同时也出于自身意愿的事情，也许就能改变母亲使用的偏颇语言。只有停止把母职说成牺牲，我们才能开始以母亲应得的方式谈论她们。

paragraphs.A: Worried about Internet companies spying on your online browsing? You might turn to something called a virtual private network to protect your privacy. But researchers say these networks can themselves be insecure.
paragraphs.B: Earlier this year, the federal government rolled back rules that would have prevented Internet service providers from tracking your activity online. Comcast, AT&T and other providers are now allowed to track and sell your personal data too—with much less fear of regulatory action.
paragraphs.C: One solution is a VPN, which is like a dark, secret tunnel you use to go from your computer to a website. While you’re inside the tunnel—clicking on Instagram photos or checking your bank account—third parties can’t see what you’re doing. There are lots of reasons people around the world use VPNs: to hide location, to access work networks, even to avoid government censorship.
paragraphs.D: Internet providers handle customer privacy in different ways. Some say you have to opt in for them to sell your data. Because of Internet-connected devices, providers can see more than the websites you browse.
paragraphs.E: So, who cares whether Time Warner Cable or Verizon knows when I turn off my lights or whether I stock my fridge with Swiss or cheddar?
paragraphs.F: For one thing, those data points can be used to target advertising. And the government or private companies could use the information to deny services, like health insurance—or even water.
paragraphs.G: Some VPNs promise anonymous browsing for free or just a few dollars a month; they claim not to share your data. But these services don’t always deliver on their promises. Sometimes the medicine might be worse than the illness. In the first major review of VPN providers, what researchers found was alarming. Nearly 40 percent injected malware.
paragraphs.H: Experts suggest researching a VPN before using it and to think of it as a supplementary tool, not a privacy solution. They advise reading the VPN service provider’s privacy policy to see whether it collects or retains any user information that could be traced back to you.

translationZh.A: 担心互联网公司窥探你的网上浏览活动？你可能会使用一种叫作虚拟专用网络的工具来保护隐私。但研究人员表示，这些网络本身也可能不安全。
translationZh.B: 在本文写作当年的早些时候，美国联邦政府撤销了一些本可阻止互联网服务提供商追踪用户在线活动的规定。康卡斯特、AT&T 等服务商因而可以追踪并出售个人数据，而且对监管措施的顾虑大大减少。
translationZh.C: 一种解决办法是使用 VPN。它就像一条从电脑通向网站的隐秘隧道。当你身处隧道之中，点击 Instagram 照片或查看银行账户时，第三方看不到你正在做什么。世界各地的人使用 VPN 的原因很多：隐藏位置、访问工作网络，甚至规避政府审查。
translationZh.D: 互联网服务商处理客户隐私的方式各不相同。有些表示，只有用户主动同意，才会出售其数据。由于各种设备联网，服务商所能看到的信息已经不只是用户浏览的网站。
translationZh.E: 那么，时代华纳有线或威瑞森知道我什么时候关灯，或者冰箱里放的是瑞士奶酪还是切达奶酪，又有什么关系呢？
translationZh.F: 首先，这些数据可以用于定向投放广告。政府或私人公司也可能利用这些信息拒绝提供服务，例如医疗保险，甚至供水。
translationZh.G: 有些 VPN 承诺免费或每月只花几美元就能匿名浏览，并声称不会分享用户数据。但这些服务并不总能兑现承诺，有时解决办法带来的问题反而更严重。在首次针对 VPN 服务商的大规模评估中，研究人员发现了令人担忧的情况：近四成会植入恶意软件。
translationZh.H: 专家建议在使用 VPN 前先进行调查，仅将其视为辅助工具，不能靠它彻底解决隐私问题。专家还建议阅读服务商的隐私政策，查看它是否收集或保留能够追溯到用户本人的信息。

title: How Politics Shapes Our View of Evidence
titleZh: 政治立场如何影响我们看待证据

paragraphs.A: Ask a left-wing Briton what they believe about the safety of nuclear power, and you can guess their answer. Ask a right-wing American about the risks posed by climate change, and you can also make a better guess than if you didn’t know their political affiliation. Issues like these feel like they should be informed by science, not our political tribes, but sadly, that’s not what happens.
paragraphs.B: Psychology has long shown that education and intelligence won’t stop your politics from shaping your broader worldview, even if those beliefs do not match the hard evidence. Instead, your ability to weigh up the facts may depend on a less well-recognised trait—curiosity.
paragraphs.C: There is now a mountain of evidence to show that politics doesn’t just help predict people’s views on some scientific issues; it also affects how they interpret new information. This is why it is a mistake to think that you can somehow “correct” people’s views on an issue by giving them more facts, since study after study has shown that people have a tendency to selectively reject facts that don’t fit with their existing views.
paragraphs.D: But smarter people shouldn’t be susceptible to prejudice swaying their opinions, right? Wrong. Other research shows that people with the most education, highest mathematical abilities, and the strongest tendencies to be reflective about their beliefs are the most likely to resist information which should contradict their prejudices. This undermines the simplistic assumption that prejudices are the result of too much gut instinct and not enough deep thought. Rather, people who have the facility for deeper thought about an issue can use those cognitive powers to justify what they already believe and find reasons to dismiss apparently contrary evidence.

translationZh.A: 问一位持左翼立场的英国人如何看待核能的安全性，你大致能猜到对方的回答。问一位持右翼立场的美国人如何看待气候变化带来的风险，知道对方的政治归属，也能让你猜得更准。按理说，这类问题上的判断应该以科学为依据，而非取决于我们所属的政治阵营。遗憾的是，实际情况并非如此。
translationZh.B: 心理学早已表明，即使你的看法与确凿的证据不符，受教育程度和智力也无法阻止政治立场影响你更广泛的世界观。相反，你能否权衡事实，或许取决于一种较少受到关注的特质——好奇心。
translationZh.C: 如今，大量证据表明，政治立场既能帮助预测人们对某些科学问题的看法，也会影响他们如何解读新信息。因此，以为只要多提供一些事实，就能以某种方式“纠正”人们对某个问题的看法，是一种错误。因为一项又一项研究表明，人们往往会有选择地排斥与自己既有观点不符的事实。
translationZh.D: 不过，更聪明的人应该不容易让偏见左右自己的看法，对吧？事实恰恰相反。其他研究表明，受教育程度最高、数学能力最强、最倾向于反思自身信念的人，反而最可能抵制本应推翻其偏见的信息。这动摇了一种过于简单的假设，即偏见源于过分依赖直觉、缺乏深入思考。事实上，善于深入思考问题的人，可以运用这些认知能力为自己早已相信的观点辩护，并找理由排斥那些看似与之相矛盾的证据。

paragraphs.A: We have to fix the internet. After 40 years, it has begun to corrode, both itself and us. It is still a marvelous and miraculous invention, but now there are bugs in the foundation, bats in the belfry, and trolls in the basement.
paragraphs.B: I do not mean this to be one of those technophobic rants insulting the internet for rewiring our brains to give us the nervous attention span of Donald Trump on Twitter or pontificating about how we have to log off and smell the flowers. Those worries about new technologies have existed ever since Plato was concerned that the technology of writing would threaten memorization and oratory. I love the internet and all of its digital offshoots. What I feel sad for is its decline.
paragraphs.C: There is a bug in its original design that at first seemed like a feature but has gradually, and now rapidly, been exploited by hackers and trolls and malevolent actors: Its packets are encoded with the address of their destination but not of their authentic origin. With a circuit-switched network, you can track or trace back the origins of the information, but that’s not true with the packet-switched design of the internet.
paragraphs.D: Compounding this was the architecture that Tim Berners-Lee and the inventors of the early browsers created for the World Wide Web. It brilliantly allowed the whole of the earth’s computers to be webbed together and navigated through hyperlinks. But the links were one-way. You knew where the links took you. But if you had a webpage or piece of content, you didn’t exactly know who was linking to you or coming to use your content.
paragraphs.E: All of that protected the potential for anonymity. You could make comments anonymously. Go to a webpage anonymously. Consume content anonymously. With a little effort, send email anonymously. And if you figured out a way to get into someone’s servers or databases, you could do it anonymously.
paragraphs.F: For years, the benefits of anonymity on the net outweighed its drawbacks. People felt more free to express themselves, which was especially valuable if they were holding different opinions or hiding a personal secret. This was celebrated in the famous 1993 New Yorker cartoon, “On the Internet, nobody knows you’re a dog.”
paragraphs.G: Now the problem is nobody can tell if you’re a troll. Or a hacker. Or a bot. Or a Macedonian teenager publishing a story that the Pope has supported Trump. This has poisoned civil discourse, enabled hacking, permitted cyberbullying, and made email a risk.
paragraphs.H: The lack of secure identification and authentication inherent in the internet’s genetic code had also prevented easy transactions, obstructed financial inclusion, destroyed the business models of content creators, unleashed the overflow of spam, and forced us to use passwords and two-factor authentication schemes that would have confused Houdini. The trillions being spent and the IQ points of computer science talent being allocated to tackle security issues make it a drag, rather than a spur, to productivity in some sectors.
paragraphs.I: In Plato’s Republic, we learn the tale of the Ring of Gyges. Put it on, and you’re invisible and anonymous. The question that Plato asks is whether those who put on the ring will be civil and moral. He thinks not. The internet has proven him correct. The web is no longer a place of community, no longer a marketplace. Every day more sites are eliminating comments sections.
paragraphs.J: If we could start from scratch, here’s what I think we would do: Create a system that enables content producers to negotiate with aggregators and search engines to get a royalty whenever their content is used, like ASCAP has negotiated for public performances and radio airings of its members’ works. Embed a simple digital wallet and currency for quick and easy small payments for songs, blogs, articles, and whatever other digital content is for sale. Encode emails with an authenticated return or originating address. Enforce critical properties and security at the lowest levels of the system possible, such as in the hardware or in the programming language, instead of leaving it to programmers to incorporate security into every line of code they write. Build chips and machines that update the notion of an internet packet. For those who want, their packets could be encoded or tagged with metadata that describe what they contain and give the rules for how it can be used.
paragraphs.K: Most internet engineers think that these reforms are possible, from Vint Cerf, the original TCP/IP coauthor, to Milo Medin of Google, to Howard Shrobe, the director of cybersecurity at MIT. “We don’t need to live in cyber hell,” Shrobe has argued. Implementing them is less a matter of technology than of cost and social will. Some people, understandably, will resist any reduction of anonymity, which they sometimes label privacy.
paragraphs.L: So the best approach, I think, would be to try to create a voluntary system, for those who want to use it, to have verified identification and authentication. People would not be forced to use such a system. If they wanted to communicate and surf anonymously, they could. But those of us who choose, at times, not to be anonymous and not to deal with people who are anonymous should have that right as well. That’s the way it works in the real world.
paragraphs.M: The benefits would be many. Easy and secure ways to deal with your finances and medical records. Small payment systems that could reward valued content rather than the current incentive to concentrate on clickbait for advertising. Less hacking, spamming, cyberbullying, trolling, and spewing of anonymous hate. And the possibility of a more civil discourse.

translationZh.A: 我们得修好互联网。四十年过去了，互联网已经开始侵蚀自身，也在侵蚀我们。它依然是一项了不起的发明，但如今就像一栋房子，地基里有虫子，钟楼里有蝙蝠，地下室里还藏着捣乱的人。
translationZh.B: 我无意像那些惧怕技术的人一样，长篇大论地骂互联网改变了我们的大脑，让我们像在推特上的唐纳德·特朗普一样，注意力短暂而容易分散。我也无意摆出说教的姿态，劝大家下线去感受生活中的美好。对新技术的担忧由来已久，柏拉图就曾担心书写技术会威胁记忆和演讲的能力。我喜爱互联网以及由它衍生的一切数字事物。我为它的衰落感到惋惜。
translationZh.C: 互联网的原始设计有一处缺陷，起初看起来像是一项功能，却逐渐被黑客、网络喷子和其他心怀恶意的人利用，如今这种利用愈演愈烈。数据包编码中有目的地地址，却没有真实的来源地址。在电路交换网络中，你可以追踪信息的来源，而互联网采用的分组交换设计做不到这一点。
translationZh.D: 蒂姆·伯纳斯-李和早期浏览器的发明者为万维网搭建的架构，又加深了这个问题。这一架构巧妙地把全球的计算机连成网络，让人们可以通过超链接浏览。但链接是单向的。你知道点击链接会去哪里，可如果你有网页或发布了内容，就很难确切知道谁链接到了你，或者谁来使用你的内容。
translationZh.E: 这一切保留了匿名的可能性。你可以匿名发表评论、访问网页、浏览内容。稍费些工夫，也可以匿名发送邮件。如果你找到进入别人服务器或数据库的办法，也可以匿名操作。
translationZh.F: 多年来，网络匿名的好处大于弊端。人们觉得表达自己更自由了，尤其是在持有不同意见或想保守个人秘密时。1993 年《纽约客》那幅著名漫画就赞扬了这一点：“在互联网上，没人知道你是一条狗。”
translationZh.G: 现在的问题是，没人能判断你是不是网络喷子、黑客、机器人，或是一个发帖声称教皇支持特朗普的马其顿青少年。这种情况破坏了文明讨论，助长了黑客活动和网络霸凌，也让电子邮件带来了风险。
translationZh.H: 互联网先天缺乏安全的身份识别和认证机制，这也使交易变得不便，阻碍了普惠金融，破坏了内容创作者的商业模式，导致垃圾邮件泛滥，还迫使我们使用连逃脱大师胡迪尼都可能被搞糊涂的密码和双因素认证方案。为解决安全问题而投入的巨额资金和计算机人才，使互联网在某些领域拖累了生产力，原本它可以促进生产力。
translationZh.I: 在柏拉图的《理想国》中，我们读到古格斯之戒的故事。戴上戒指，你就能隐身，别人也无从知道你的身份。柏拉图问，戴上戒指的人还会讲文明、守道德吗？他认为不会。互联网印证了他的判断。网络已失去作为社群和市场的功能。每天都有更多网站关掉评论区。
translationZh.J: 如果可以从头来过，我认为可以这样做。建立一个系统，让内容创作者同内容聚合平台和搜索引擎谈判，使自己的内容每次被使用时都能获得版税，就像美国作曲家、作家与出版商协会为会员作品的公开演出和电台播放争取报酬一样。嵌入简单的数字钱包和货币，方便人们为歌曲、博客、文章及其他出售的数字内容快速进行小额支付。让电子邮件带有经过认证的回复地址或发件地址。尽可能在系统底层保障关键属性和安全，例如在硬件或编程语言中落实这些要求，让安全性由底层提供，免去程序员在每一行代码里单独处理的负担。开发能够更新互联网数据包设计的芯片和机器。有需要的人可以为自己的数据包编码或添加元数据，说明数据包里有什么，以及其中的内容可按什么规则使用。
translationZh.K: 多数互联网工程师认为，这些改革在技术上可行，包括 TCP/IP 的共同设计者文特·瑟夫、谷歌的米洛·梅丁，以及麻省理工学院负责网络安全的霍华德·施罗布。施罗布说过：“我们没必要活在网络地狱里。”实施改革主要取决于成本和社会意愿。有些人会抵制任何对匿名性的削减，这可以理解。他们有时把匿名性称为隐私。
translationZh.L: 因此，我认为最好的办法是建立一套自愿使用的系统，让愿意使用的人能够验证身份。人们可以自行选择。想匿名交流和上网的人仍然可以这么做。有些时候，我们也会选择表明身份，并只与身份可核实的人打交道，这样做也应当是我们的权利。现实世界正是这样运作的。
translationZh.M: 这样做会有许多好处。人们可以更方便、更安全地管理财务和医疗记录。小额支付系统可以让有价值的内容得到回报，改变目前为赚广告费而追逐标题党的激励机制。黑客攻击、垃圾信息、网络霸凌、恶意挑衅和匿名仇恨言论也可能减少，网络讨论有望变得更文明。

title: Busyness as a Status Symbol
titleZh: 忙碌为何成了身份象征

paragraphs.A: One of my bad habits is saying “busy” when people ask me how I’m doing. Sometimes it’s because I actually am busy, but other times it’s because that’s what I think I’m supposed to say. That’s what important people say. That’s what people who get promoted say. But working long hours doesn’t drive better results. Never taking a vacation won’t lead to a promotion. So why are we so proud to talk about how busy we are all the time?
paragraphs.B: In 2016, researchers from Columbia, Harvard, and Georgetown conducted a study to figure it out. They found busy people are perceived to be of high status, and interestingly, these status attributions are heavily influenced by our own beliefs about social mobility. In other words, the more we believe that one has the opportunity for success based on hard work, the more we tend to think that people who skip leisure and work all the time are of higher standing.
paragraphs.C: That’s why we feel like we have to appear busy, and there’s a real perception that if someone is knee-deep in meetings, emails and stress, then they’re probably a big deal. This culture of busyness is making it hard for employees to find work-life balance. According to a recent study, one in five highly engaged employees are at risk of burnout.
paragraphs.D: Personally, I’m going to stop saying “busy” when people ask me how I am. It sounds self-righteous and sets the wrong tone. Phrases like “I have limited access to email” and “I’ll respond as soon as I get back” sound like you’re being held against your will from working as opposed to making the most of your time off.
paragraphs.E: That’s why we recently launched the Out of Office Email Generator, a free tool you can use before your next long weekend or trip. You can share loud and proud that you won’t be checking email until you’re back. Managers need to think twice about emailing their teams on the weekend and talking about how busy they are. Leaders should take time off themselves and encourage employees to do the same.

translationZh.A: 我的一个坏习惯是，别人问我近况如何时，我总说“忙”。有时是因为我确实很忙，但有时是因为我觉得自己就应该这样回答。重要的人都这么说，得到晋升的人都这么说。然而，长时间工作并不能带来更好的成果，从不休假也不会让你获得晋升。那么，我们为什么总是如此自豪地谈论自己有多忙呢？
translationZh.B: 2016 年，来自哥伦比亚大学、哈佛大学和乔治敦大学的研究人员开展了一项研究，试图弄清这个问题。他们发现，人们认为忙碌的人社会地位较高。有趣的是，这种地位判断在很大程度上受我们自身对社会流动性的看法影响。换句话说，我们越相信一个人有机会通过努力工作取得成功，就越倾向于认为那些放弃休闲、一直工作的人地位更高。
translationZh.C: 这就是为什么我们觉得自己必须表现得很忙。而且，人们确实普遍认为：如果一个人深陷会议、电子邮件和压力之中，那他大概是个重要人物。这种推崇忙碌的文化，使员工难以在工作与生活之间找到平衡。根据最近的一项研究，每五名工作投入度很高的员工中，就有一名面临职业倦怠的风险。
translationZh.D: 就我个人而言，别人再问我近况如何时，我不会再说“忙”了。这样的回答听起来自以为是，也传递了不恰当的态度。“我不方便经常查看邮件”和“我一回来就会回复”之类的话，听起来仿佛你是被迫无法工作，而不是在充分利用自己的休假时光。
translationZh.E: 这就是我们最近推出“休假自动回复邮件生成器”的原因。这是一款免费工具，你可以在下一次长周末或旅行前使用。你完全可以大大方方、自豪地告诉别人：回来之前，你不会查看邮件。管理者在周末给团队发邮件，或谈论自己有多忙之前，都应该三思。领导者应当自己带头休假，并鼓励员工也这样做。

title: Business Travel and the Gender Gap in Airfares
titleZh: 商务旅行中的机票价格性别差异
source: User-provided CET-4 reading · December 2023 · Paper 1 · Passage Two. Descriptive title added for navigation.

paragraphs.A: Female employees consistently pay lower airfares than men do for the same flights because they tend to book earlier.
paragraphs.B: We compared the airfare paid by employees in the same position within a company for the same class of travel and used a common statistical technique to account for other factors that might affect differences in airfares. We found that women paid on average $18 less per ticket than their male colleagues. Further investigation allowed us to conclude that this gap is largely explained by the fact that women tended to book earlier than men, 1.8 days on average.
paragraphs.C: We wanted to determine what was causing these gender differences in booking business trips so we tested a variety of possible explanations, such as women choosing to plan ahead or male frequent travelers being inclined to book late. None of these explained away the gender gap, so we applied data collected from surveys that express consumer preferences that play a central role in economic decisions, such as patience and risk avoidance.
paragraphs.D: We found that only the concept of “negative reciprocity”—in which an employee who feels unfairly treated engages in negative behaviors, such as spending their company’s money less carefully—explains these differences. The surveys showed men tend to exhibit more of these negative behaviors than women.
paragraphs.E: This isn’t to say that all men engage in these behaviors—or that booking relatively late is a sign of abnormal behavior. It only means that the gender gap disappears when we plug in the negative reciprocity variable.
paragraphs.F: Prior research on negative reciprocity among workers found that it can result in lower employee motivation, business performance and workplace morale and culture.
paragraphs.G: Our results show another way these negative behaviors can manifest themselves, like in airline bookings, and add to evidence that women are less likely to engage in them.
paragraphs.H: Companies spend significant sums of money on business travel. While that $18 difference per ticket may seem small, it adds up. Our analysis suggests early booking by women can translate into savings of $1 million a year for a large multinational company with 20,000 regular travelers.

translationZh.A: 女性员工乘坐相同航班时，支付的机票价格通常比男性低，因为她们往往更早订票。
translationZh.B: 我们比较了同一家公司中职位相同的员工乘坐相同舱等时支付的机票价格，并采用一种常见的统计方法，控制其他可能影响机票价格差异的因素。我们发现，女性每张机票平均比男同事少支付18美元。进一步调查使我们得出结论：这一差距在很大程度上可以用女性通常比男性更早订票来解释，平均提前1.8天。
translationZh.C: 我们想确定，预订商务旅行时出现这些性别差异的原因是什么，因此检验了多种可能的解释，例如女性选择提前规划，或者经常出差的男性倾向于较晚订票。这些解释都未能消除性别差距，因此我们使用了调查收集的数据。这些数据反映了消费者的偏好，而耐心和风险规避等偏好在经济决策中起着核心作用。
translationZh.D: 我们发现，只有“负向互惠”这一概念能够解释这些差异：当员工觉得自己受到不公平对待时，会采取负面行为，例如花公司的钱时不那么谨慎。调查显示，男性往往比女性表现出更多此类负面行为。
translationZh.E: 这并不是说所有男性都会采取这些行为，也不是说相对较晚订票就是行为异常的表现。这仅仅意味着，当我们将负向互惠这一变量纳入分析时，性别差距就消失了。
translationZh.F: 此前有关员工负向互惠的研究发现，它可能降低员工的工作积极性和企业的经营表现，并损害工作场所的士气和文化。
translationZh.G: 我们的结果展示了这些负面行为的另一种表现方式，例如在预订机票方面；同时也提供了更多证据，表明女性较少采取这些行为。
translationZh.H: 企业在商务旅行上花费大量资金。每张机票18美元的差价看似不大，但累积起来数额可观。我们的分析表明，对于一家拥有两万名经常出差员工的大型跨国公司来说，女性提前订票所带来的节省，一年可以达到100万美元。

paragraphs.A: A number of studies have looked at how family life can affect productivity and satisfaction in the workplace. However, there has been surprisingly little research on the influence of leisure activities. So Ciara Kelly and colleagues recruited 129 hobbyists to look at how the time spent on their hobbies shaped their work life.
paragraphs.B: The researchers found that when participants spent longer than normal on their leisure activity, their belief in their ability to perform their job was strengthened. But this was only the case when they had a serious hobby that was dissimilar to their job, or when their hobby was similar to their work but they only did it casually. When their hobby was both serious and similar to their job, then spending more time on it actually decreased their work efficiency.
paragraphs.C: Why might that be? To maintain a serious hobby, people need to invest significant psychological resources, say the authors—so if the activity has the same kinds of demands as their work, they may be left exhausted and unable to perform well at their job. But if their hobby is quite different from their career, it may not interfere in the same way but instead help them develop other knowledge and skills that can boost their confidence at work. “Consider a scientist who is a keen rock climber,” says Kelly. “Since climbing is so far removed from their day-to-day work activities, they can still recover from the demands of their job with plenty of resources.”

translationZh.A: 许多研究考察了家庭生活如何影响工作场所中的生产效率和满意度。然而，关于休闲活动影响的研究却少得令人惊讶。因此，席亚拉·凯利及其同事招募了129名业余爱好者，考察他们花在兴趣爱好上的时间如何影响其工作生活。
translationZh.B: 研究人员发现，当参与者花在休闲活动上的时间比平时更长时，他们对自己胜任工作的能力更有信心。但这种情况只出现在以下两种情形：他们认真投入的爱好与工作不同；或者爱好与工作相似，但他们只是随意地参与。当他们既认真投入爱好，而爱好又与工作相似时，在爱好上花更多时间实际上会降低工作效率。
translationZh.C: 为什么会这样呢？作者指出，要维持一项认真投入的爱好，人们需要投入大量心理资源。因此，如果这项活动与工作提出的要求相同，他们就可能变得筋疲力尽，无法在工作中表现良好。但如果爱好与职业有很大不同，它可能就不会以同样的方式干扰工作，反而能帮助他们掌握其他知识和技能，从而增强工作中的自信。凯利说：“想想一位热衷攀岩的科学家。由于攀岩与他们的日常工作活动相去甚远，他们仍能从工作带来的消耗中恢复过来，并保有充足的资源。”

title: More Fathers Are Taking Paternity Leave, But Mothers Are Still Doing All the Work
titleZh: 更多父亲开始休陪产假，但母亲仍承担全部重担
source: User-provided CET-4 · December 2023 · Paper 2 · Section B · pages 13–14. Historical claims and figures preserved from the printed passage.

paragraphs.A: Attitudes towards paternity leave (陪产假) have drastically changed in America in the last five years as more fathers feel comfortable taking extended time off, but gender bias persists when it comes to career prospects and the home, according to a new study of working parents.
paragraphs.B: Research by the Boston College Center for Work & Family, which surveyed new parents at four large U.S. companies who were qualified for taking at least six weeks paid parental leave, found that 81% of the 1,240 employees surveyed said the notion of fathers taking leave has become more acceptable.
paragraphs.C: Of those surveyed, 62% of fathers took the maximum amount of time off compared to 93% of mothers, and around three-quarters of workers said their employer was equally supportive of mothers and fathers taking parental leave and over half said leave policies had made workplace culture better.
paragraphs.D: The U.S. is one of only three countries in the world not to offer statutory (法定的) paid leave, but increasingly states and companies are starting to take up the issue. So far, eight states and the District of Columbia have their own paid family leave laws.
paragraphs.E: Brad Harrington, executive director of the center and lead author of the study, estimates only 20% to 30% of companies in the U.S. offer paid parental leave. He feels the research findings reflect an obvious change in corporate attitudes to new fathers taking time off.
paragraphs.F: “We did a study on paternity leave five years ago. Compared with those findings, these numbers were shocking to me. I did not expect 80% of people to say the organisation finds dads taking this leave acceptable and three-quarters to say it’s equally supportive of women and men taking leave,” Harrington said.
paragraphs.G: The previous study found that nearly three-quarters of fathers saw two to four weeks as an appropriate duration for paternity leave and 76% said they would prefer not to take all their time off at once.
paragraphs.H: Since then, there have been a number of legal cases against companies involving paternity leave—including cases against JPMorgan Chase and Estée Lauder—which have helped put pressure on companies to make their parental leave policies gender neutral.
paragraphs.I: However, the study also shows how traditional gender roles endure both at work, where more women than men reported changes in their perceived career potential, and at home—even among workers who claim to have a strong desire for equality.
paragraphs.J: The vast majority of men, 97%, said one of the top reasons to take leave was to share caregiving with their partner. But when they were asked about how caregiving and household tasks were divided, their answers painted a different picture. While about 75% of employees said both genders should give the same amount of care, the majority of men and nearly half of women admitted that in reality the female actually did most of it. A tiny fraction, 2%, of men said they did more of the childcare.
paragraphs.K: Men and women’s experiences of the return to work following parental leave were also considerably different. Of the women surveyed, 32% reported a downturn in their job satisfaction, while 14% said it increased. In comparison, 17% of men said their job satisfaction went down and 20% said it went up. Meanwhile, more women reported an increase in their responsibilities and manager expectations after childbirth. Half of the women said they used flexible work arrangements after becoming a parent, while just 27% of men did. Similar percentages of men and women said they enjoyed their careers and that it gave them a sense of achievement, while around half of women and 44% of men said it was a key part of their identity.
paragraphs.L: On the subject of career advancement, 59% of women and 49% of men said leave could be limiting and both genders said they feared it would have an impact on their progress long-term. But on opportunity for promotion, more than double the number of women, 30% compared with 15% of men, believed their chances to be lower after becoming a parent. Despite progress, the struggle for women to reach the highest positions of power is demonstrated in this year’s Fortune 500 list, which featured a record 33 female CEOs, but this still represents a tiny fraction of the total.
paragraphs.M: Harrington said culture change depends on companies putting more focus on men and their responsibilities. “By that I mean companies need to give men paternity leave and encourage men to take time off to be with their kids early on in the kids’ life. They also need to recognise that men have to make significant adjustments when they become parents. Companies cannot do all these things to enhance women’s advancement and then turn around and say, ‘Oh, but we don’t expect the men to take over for the women at home.’”
paragraphs.N: In May, the American Civil Liberties Union (ACLU) and Outten & Golden LLP announced a historic class-action $5m settlement with JPMorgan Chase on behalf of male employees who claim they were illegally denied access to paid parental leave. Derek Rotondo, 35, filed the discrimination charge against his company after he was allegedly told by his HR department that mothers were considered primary caregivers. Thus, they were allowed to take 16 weeks of paid parental leave. Fathers, however, could take just two weeks.
paragraphs.O: The father of two from Columbus, Ohio, who still works at the company as an associate and investigator, said he has witnessed a “domino effect (多米诺效应)” across companies since the settlement, but that there is still substantial progress to be made towards changing attitudes towards paternity leave.
paragraphs.P: “I do think there’s still some way to go…there’s still going to be sort of the unstated expectation for new dads to essentially come right back to work, but I think the research is showing that’s starting to change.” He said equal parental leave is an essential component to creating gender equality in the workplace. “The old standard of women staying home, having babies and cooking doesn’t apply and hasn’t applied for a long time.”

translationZh.A: 一项针对在职父母的新研究显示，过去五年间，美国人对陪产假的态度发生了巨大变化，越来越多的父亲能够安心休较长的假期，但在职业前景和家庭生活方面，性别偏见依然存在。
translationZh.B: 波士顿学院工作与家庭研究中心调查了美国四家大公司的新晋父母，这些人都符合享受至少六周带薪育儿假的条件。研究发现，在接受调查的1,240名员工中，81%表示，父亲休假的观念已变得更容易被接受。
translationZh.C: 在受访者中，62%的父亲休满了可享受的假期，而母亲的比例为93%。约四分之三的员工表示，雇主同样支持母亲和父亲休育儿假；超过一半的人表示，休假政策改善了职场文化。
translationZh.D: 美国是世界上仅有的三个不提供法定带薪假的国家之一，但越来越多的州和企业开始着手处理这一问题。截至文章所述时间，八个州和哥伦比亚特区已制定各自的带薪家庭假法律。
translationZh.E: 该中心执行主任、研究第一作者布拉德·哈林顿估计，美国只有20%至30%的企业提供带薪育儿假。他认为，研究结果反映出企业对新晋父亲休假的态度出现了明显变化。
translationZh.F: 哈林顿说：“我们五年前做过一项有关陪产假的研究。与那时的结果相比，这些数字令我震惊。我没有想到，80%的人会说所在机构认为父亲休这种假可以接受，四分之三的人会说，机构同样支持女性和男性休假。”
translationZh.G: 此前的研究发现，近四分之三的父亲认为，两至四周是合适的陪产假时长；76%表示，他们更愿意不一次性休完全部假期。
translationZh.H: 此后，出现了多起涉及陪产假的企业诉讼，其中包括针对摩根大通和雅诗兰黛的案件。这些案件推动企业制定不因性别而有所区别的育儿假政策。
translationZh.I: 然而，研究也显示，传统性别角色在职场和家庭中仍然存在。在职场，报告自己所感知的职业发展潜力发生变化的女性多于男性；在家中，即使那些声称强烈追求平等的员工，也仍受传统性别角色影响。
translationZh.J: 绝大多数男性，即97%，表示休假的主要原因之一是与伴侣共同承担照护责任。但当被问及照护和家务如何分配时，他们的回答却呈现出另一幅景象。尽管约75%的员工认为男女应该承担同等的照护工作，多数男性和近半数女性承认，现实中女性实际上承担了大部分工作。只有极少数男性，即2%，表示自己承担了更多育儿工作。
translationZh.K: 男女休完育儿假返岗后的经历也有很大差异。在受访女性中，32%表示工作满意度下降，14%表示上升。相比之下，17%的男性表示工作满意度下降，20%表示上升。同时，更多女性表示，生育后工作职责和上司对自己的期望增加了。一半女性表示，成为父母后采用了灵活的工作安排，而男性仅有27%。表示喜欢自己的职业、并从中获得成就感的男女比例相近；约一半女性和44%的男性表示，职业是自我身份的重要组成部分。
translationZh.L: 关于职业发展，59%的女性和49%的男性表示，休假可能带来限制；男女都担心，这会对自己的长期发展产生影响。但在晋升机会方面，30%的女性认为成为父母后机会会减少，男性的比例为15%；原文写作“两倍多”，但所列30%恰为15%的两倍。尽管已有进步，女性要达到最高权力职位仍然困难：文章所述当年的《财富》美国500强榜单中，女性首席执行官达到创纪录的33人，但仍仅占总数的极小一部分。
translationZh.M: 哈林顿说，文化的改变取决于企业更多关注男性及其责任。“我的意思是，企业需要给男性陪产假，鼓励他们在孩子出生后不久休假陪伴孩子。企业还需要认识到，男性成为父母时也必须作出重大调整。企业不能一方面采取这些措施促进女性的职业发展，另一方面又说：‘哦，但我们并不指望男性在家中接替女性的工作。’”
translationZh.N: 五月，美国公民自由联盟和奥滕与戈尔登律师事务所宣布，代表声称被非法剥夺带薪育儿假权利的男性员工，与摩根大通达成了一项具有历史意义、金额为500万美元的集体诉讼和解。据称，35岁的德里克·罗通多被人力资源部门告知，母亲被视为主要照护者，因此可以享受16周带薪育儿假，而父亲只能休两周。此后，他针对公司提出了歧视指控。
translationZh.O: 这位来自俄亥俄州哥伦布市的两个孩子的父亲，仍在该公司担任助理和调查员。他说，和解之后，他已看到各家公司之间出现“多米诺效应”，但在改变对陪产假的态度方面，仍有很大的进步空间。
translationZh.P: “我确实认为还有一段路要走……人们仍会对新晋父亲抱有某种未明说的期待，认为他们基本上应该立即回去工作。不过，我认为研究表明，这种情况正在开始改变。”他说，平等的育儿假是实现职场性别平等的重要组成部分。“女性待在家里、生孩子、做饭的旧标准已经不适用了，而且早已不适用了。”

title: Rivalry and Entrepreneurial Decision-Making
source: User-provided CET-4 · December 2023 · Paper 2 · Passage One. Descriptive title and paragraph labels added for navigation; article body only, no questions or answers.

paragraphs.A: Having a rival can keep you committed to achieving your goals and enhance your overall performance. But before you go out and find an entrepreneur to outcompete, it’s important to understand and avoid the traps that often come with rivalry. After all, competitive rivalry can also hinder effective decision-making and increase your willingness to take risks, behaviors that can ultimately hurt your venture’s success.
paragraphs.B: Finding someone you’re committed to outcompeting can be a great way to stay focused on your goals and push your venture to the next level. But when you’re intently focused on outperforming your rivals, you may begin to develop a “win-at-all-costs” mentality that causes you to ignore how you achieve success. One group of researchers, for example, examined the link between rivalry and unethical behavior. They found that when people compete against their rivals, they are more willing to behave unethically to win. But such behavior may stain your reputation and strain relationships important to your success. One way to avoid this trap is to stop and reflect on what’s important. While outperforming your rivals may provide short-term benefits, the loss of your integrity will have long-term consequences.
paragraphs.C: One reason having a rival can enhance your venture’s performance is that it creates a level of excitement that drives you to work harder. But this eagerness to win may also hurt your venture’s success, particularly when it causes you to make impulsive, insensible decisions. But it’s possible to avoid such costly mistakes by making a habit of engaging in critical thinking, such as considering opposing viewpoints and conducting cost-benefit analyses, especially for those decisions that are complex and can determine the future of your venture.
paragraphs.D: The sense of eagerness that comes with having a rival can not only cause you to make poorer decisions, but it can also lead you to take greater risks that put your venture in peril. One way you can overcome the risk-inducing effects of rivalry that stand to endanger your venture’s success is to remain attentive to your emotional state and actively monitor how such feelings are affecting your decision-making.

translationZh.A: 有一个竞争对手，可以让你坚持实现目标，并提升整体表现。但在你着手寻找一位企业家作为超越对象之前，重要的是理解并避开竞争常常伴随的陷阱。毕竟，竞争也可能妨碍有效决策，增加你冒险的意愿，而这些行为最终可能损害你的创业事业。
translationZh.B: 找到一个你决心超越的人，是保持目标专注、推动事业更上一层楼的好办法。但当你一心只想着胜过对手时，可能会逐渐形成一种“不惜一切代价取胜”的心态，让你忽视自己是如何取得成功的。例如，一组研究人员考察了竞争关系与不道德行为之间的联系。他们发现，人们与自己的竞争对手较量时，更愿意为了获胜而采取不道德的行为。然而，这样做可能损害你的声誉，使对成功至关重要的人际关系变得紧张。避免这一陷阱的一个办法，是停下来思考什么才真正重要。虽然胜过竞争对手可能带来短期利益，但丧失诚信会产生长期后果。
translationZh.C: 竞争对手之所以能提升你的事业表现，一个原因是竞争会带来一定程度的兴奋，促使你更加努力。但这种求胜的急切心情也可能损害事业的成功，尤其是在它使你作出冲动、不明智的决定时。不过，你可以通过养成批判性思考的习惯来避免这些代价高昂的错误，例如考虑不同立场的观点、进行成本收益分析，尤其是在作出复杂且可能决定事业未来的决策时。
translationZh.D: 拥有竞争对手带来的急切感，不仅可能使你作出更糟糕的决定，还可能让你承担更大的风险，使事业陷入险境。要克服竞争所带来的、可能危及事业成功的冒险倾向，一种办法是始终留意自己的情绪状态，并主动观察这些感受正在如何影响你的决策。

title: Multitasking: Ability, Perception, and Performance
titleZh: 多任务处理：能力、认知与表现
source: User-provided CET-4 · December 2023 · Paper 2 · Passage Two. Descriptive title and paragraph labels added for navigation. Article only; examination questions and answers excluded.

paragraphs.A: A multitasker is one who can perform two or more tasks effectively at the same time, which—apart from the obvious differences—is similar to what a computer does. The concept does indeed come from the realms of technology, where it is used to refer to an operating system that can execute multiple tasks at the same time. However, the question is: can a person really be a multitasker?
paragraphs.B: For most scientists, the answer is no. So much so that, according to experts in neuroscience (神经系统科学), our brains do not handle multitasking situations well. As soon as two tasks require our attention, productivity suffers. What we call multitasking, therefore, is in reality the ability to move more or less quickly from one task to another. This requires two essential conditions: that one of the tasks needs to be automatic, like walking or eating, and that they both need different mental processes. Answering the phone and writing at the same time, for example.
paragraphs.C: However, on the other side of the coin there are people who maintain that it is possible to be, or at least seem to be, multitasking. A recent study concluded that regardless of whether people are actually handling several tasks or not, the mere fact that they perceive this activity as multitasking has a positive effect on their performance.
paragraphs.D: The business perspective offers a different view: multitasking is understood as the ability to adapt to all types of environment within a company and effectively undertake different activities within a set time frame. Indeed, many companies look for people who are skilled in multitasking to improve their productivity. From this different perspective, you can not only be multitasking but this ability can also be taught: something that is easier in fluid organisations, which favour flexibility in their working practices.
paragraphs.E: The benefits of multitasking are clear. Being quicker and more efficient increases our performance and the number of tasks completed. But having to pay attention to several things at once means that the powers of concentration are reduced and that can lead to more mistakes.

translationZh.A: 多任务处理者，是指能够同时有效完成两项或更多任务的人。除去显而易见的差异，这与计算机所做的事情相似。这一概念确实来自技术领域，在那里，它被用来指能够同时执行多项任务的操作系统。然而，问题是：一个人真的能成为多任务处理者吗？
translationZh.B: 对多数科学家而言，答案是否定的。神经科学专家甚至指出，我们的大脑并不善于处理多任务情境。一旦两项任务都需要我们投入注意力，生产效率就会受到影响。因此，我们所谓的多任务处理，实际上是在不同任务之间或快或慢地切换的能力。这需要满足两个基本条件：其中一项任务必须能够自动进行，例如走路或吃饭；两项任务还必须需要不同的心理加工过程。比如，一边接电话，一边写字。
translationZh.C: 然而，从另一方面看，也有人坚持认为，同时处理多项任务是可能的，或者至少可以表现得像在同时处理多项任务。最近一项研究得出结论：无论人们实际上是否在处理多项任务，只要他们把这种活动看作多任务处理，就会对其表现产生积极影响。
translationZh.D: 商业领域提供了另一种视角：多任务处理被理解为，在公司内适应各种环境、并在规定时间内有效开展不同活动的能力。事实上，许多公司会寻找擅长多任务处理的人，以提高生产效率。从这一视角看，你不仅可以进行多任务处理，而且这种能力也能够通过教学培养出来。在灵活多变的组织中，做到这一点更容易，因为这类组织推崇灵活的工作方式。
translationZh.E: 多任务处理的好处显而易见。速度更快、效率更高，可以提升我们的表现，并增加完成的任务数量。然而，同时关注几件事意味着专注力会下降，而这可能导致更多错误。
